That buildspec omits the default's `export PATH="$CODEBUILD_SRC_DIR/bin:$PATH"`, so the packaged `bin/isolab-eks-mcp` is not on PATH. `run-command` already carries this export with a comment; `run-request` did not.

## BTN prime study (#2888): lean A1 (duplicate validity check removed)

`input_point` validates A1, then `point_add` validates −A1, which holds exactly when A1 is valid (same x; `modular_subtract` makes y canonical; (−y)² = y²). Added a `lean` variant building A1 from raw input words, and a `lean` mode comparing it with the combined derived network (pruning on/off, brute force, checked witness) on p = 5, 7, 11, 13 at τ = s, s/2, s/4, s/8 (32 instances). Edges 16,905→14,340 (d=3), 29,329→24,540 (d=4). All counts exact both ways, all witnesses checked. Best-of-pruning steps: lean 1.08–1.66× faster at τ ≤ s/4, 0.59–0.91× (slower) at τ ≥ s/2. Report section, README, report.json (`lean`) updated.

Report as threshold-dependent. The slowdown at large τ is because the curve check, which rejects most (x, y) pairs, then runs only inside `point_add`, after the hash and subtraction. Realistic factor bases (τ/s ≈ 2^-66 at ECCp-131) sit in the lean regime.

Crate port (derived last slot, adaptive pruning, lean first slot): paired crypto/cryptanalysis change.

## BTN prime study (#2888): held-out pruning-plan rule

Merged main (with #3522) into the #2888 branch so the study tool builds against the derived-last-slot crate. Added `rulecheck`: counts the crate's `decomposition_network` and the general network (semantic-cut path) with the pruning plan on and off, and checks the rule "build the plan only when 2^(free bits)·8 ≥ edges". p = 5, 13 (sizes used to choose the rule) and p = 67, 131 (d = 7, 8, held out), τ = s and s/8: correct in 11 of 12, worst 1.01× the best choice (p=67, τ=s), all counts agree. Where the rule switches the plan off on the crate's network: 1.83×, 3.84×, 1.28×, 1.53× fewer charged steps. Report, README, report.json (`pruning_rule`) updated.

Only a small-instance gain: at cryptographic sizes the rule always builds the plan. Worth porting to `Counter` as a default (counts unchanged).

Crate port of the rule; cryptanalysis mirror re-sync.

First attempt edited the wrong checkout (the study tool is only on the #2888 branch); disk fell to 153 MB, freed by removing the clippy debug build.

## Pruning-plan rule tried in the crate and dropped

Added `Counter::adaptive_pruning` (default on: build the plan only when 2^(free bits)·8 ≥ edges) to `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/contraction.rs`, a README note and a test on the tiny decomposition network (counts and witness equal the forced-plan control, all 2^free assignments visited, fewer charged steps). The 23 contraction tests and the new test passed, but the full suite failed one test: `tests/structured.rs` `exact_counts_and_prefix_witnesses_match_all_subgroup_targets_with_and_without_messages` hit `Limit("parsimonious program evaluation")` on the isogeny-fibre `Prepared` network at arity 3 (arity 2 passed). With the plan off its count exceeded the 500,000,000-step budget.

Dropped the crate change (never pushed) instead of weakening the test. A rule that sees only network size cannot predict per-assignment evaluation cost, which differs by network family. #2888's report and README now record the counterexample.

A sound rule would need a cost estimate per assignment (for example program steps until the first input-independent check), not edges alone.

The held-out check covered only decomposition networks; the crate's other network family was the counterexample.

## hashed-ecdl-tensor: derive the last slot in decomposition_network

### What was done
Branch `claude/hashed-ecdl-derived-last-slot` from main f465f2fb1. `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/reduction.rs`: for cofactor one and the non-semantic-cut path, `decomposition_network` now builds slots 1..m−1 as free input points (each hash-checked before its addition, as before) and computes `A_m = target − (A_1+…+A_{m−1})` with `modular_subtract` and `point_add`, then hash-checks and marks it like every other slot. Same language (bijection), so counts and the canonical witness are unchanged; free input bits drop from 2wm to 2w(m−1). The cofactor and semantic-cut paths are untouched. New test `derived_last_slot_matches_general_network_and_brute_force` (m=2 at three thresholds over every subgroup target, m=3 at one threshold): counts equal to the general network (semantic-cut path) and to an independent brute force, identical canonical witnesses, fewer free bits. Full crate suite: 140 tests pass (`cargo test --locked --release`). `cargo fmt --check` clean. Clippy clean except a pre-existing `clippy::manual_option_zip` in `src/canonical.rs` that only rustc 1.97's clippy reports (main's CI passes). End to end on `examples/fixture.json` (seed 1): scalar 4 in both, certificates byte-identical (13 relations, `verify` passes), charged steps 30,951,678 → 3,486,804 (8.9×), functional assignments 3,835 → 559; unisolated wall time 14.4 s → 1.05 s, a diagnostic only.

Default-on: outputs are identical, only the work drops. Cofactor > 1 keeps the general path because its free `S_i` preimage multiplicity would otherwise change raw counts. ## 2026-11-06 — ECC2K-130 per-link invariant guess at m = 4, degree 3

### What was done (commands, files, features)

PR #3504 (second-link guess, m = 3) merged after a pcc-gate fix (claim re-filed with a JSON validator report). Pilot: every m = 4 cell that fits 16 GB refutes at degree 4 unguessed; degree 3 needs 13–15 guesses at (12,5). With the owner's choice of k = 10, pre-registered `research/dreg_m4_link_guess_d3_20261106/`; `dreg_linear_guess` gained `--link j:k=c` (any link, `topI` coordinates from the basis); new native scorer `examples/dreg_m4_link_score.rs`. Ran all 1024 branches of both arms on 8 unsatisfiable draws (16:33–17:13 UTC). Scorer: valid; I 1888/8192, R 1312/8192; I > R on 4 draws, R > I on 3; p = 1.0, no detected difference. Report, graph, PDFs, validator report, claim PCC-20261106-6052e8 (not_covered), notes and scoreboard paragraph.

## 2026-11-06T23:30:00Z — Binary vs prime polynomial systems: matched-prime PKM run; C1 degree-5 closure started

### What was done
- The user asked whether prime-field and binary curves differ in their polynomial systems in a way that can be exploited. Read the lead atlas (crypto-autoresearcher `knowledge/leads/ecdlp`):
  - the difference is Weil descent with an F_2-linear Frobenius, which binary curves have and F_p does not;
  - the prime side is closed (`LEAD-ICE-prime-field-semaev-solving-degree`);
  - the binary side's open question is whether the solving degree stays constant (`LEAD-ICE-descent-closure-degree-at-scale`), with the `C1` cell blocked at 217 GB dense.
- The user chose both follow-ups.
- **Prime side.** `examples/pkm_tower_pilot.rs` (m = 2, Kummer, tower and null) ran on primes matched to the depth: t = 5–9, p = 2,081 to 524,801. D was 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, the same as the fixed-prime staircase, and the null gave the same D at every t. Written up in `research/pkm_matched_prime_20261106/`.
- **Binary side.** `examples/dreg_closure --sparse 5` started on `C1` draw 0 (`research/dreg_closure_scale_20261016/draws/m3-19-7.jsonl`) under a 14 GB address limit. It was at 5.5 GB after 65 min and still running.

### Decisions made
- The prime-field lead stays closed: the slope is +0.2 per step and the system equals the null.
- `C1`: the sparse closure is tried first. If it caps, a degree-capped Boolean F4 is the remaining route, at several days' work, and the user is asked first.

### Open threads
- The `C1` sparse closure result, then draws 3, 5 and 7 if draw 0 completes.

- sympy `factorint(limit=10**7)` on p±1; the large cofactors are left unfactored beyond the limit but were reported as a single factor (verified output, not primality-tested). Script: scratchpad `pm1.py`.
- P-256 p-1 = 2·3·5²·17·257·641·1531·65537·490463·6700417·(160-bit); smooth part about 2^96.
- P-256 p+1 = 2^96·7·274177·(46-bit)·(94-bit). A 2^96 subgroup exists.
- secp256k1 p-1 = 2·3·7·13441·(237-bit); smooth part about 2^19.
- secp256k1 p+1 = 2^4·7322137·(230-bit); smooth part about 2^27.
- Sources checked: KB not queried; ecdb not queried (plain arithmetic).

### Decisions made (and why)
- Only a factor table; no claim about attack viability. Whether a subgroup of size near p^(1/m) is usable depends on the V-structure the idea assumes; not tested.

- sympy not installed; installed with pip.

## 04:25Z — Lift-dense conjugate-pair family (Claude)

### What was done
- The owner asked for the conjugate-pair family, the last unchecked claim from the other session.

  - with full 2-torsion, put x₀ = e_c − γu and w = 1/u; then "t_c ∈ F_{q^{n/2}}, t_b = σ^k(t_a)" is one F_q-linear system in (w, γ);
  - n = 4 gives 6 lines, n = 6 gives 12(q+1), and n = 2 gives none generically.

  - C5 PASS: column collisions at chance (75 against 81.1, 101 against 116.2), with the planted control exact.

- **Binary side.** `examples/dreg_closure --sparse 5` started on `C1` draw 0 (`research/dreg_closure_scale_20261016/draws/m3-19-7.jsonl`) under a 14 GB address limit. It was at 5.5 GB after 65 min and still running.

- The prime-field lead stays closed: the slope is +0.2 per step and the system equals the null.

## 04:25Z — Lift-dense conjugate-pair family (Claude)

### What was done
- The owner asked for the conjugate-pair family, the last unchecked claim from the other session.
- Derived the construction before data:
  - with full 2-torsion, put x₀ = e_c − γu and w = 1/u; then "t_c ∈ F_{q^{n/2}}, t_b = σ^k(t_a)" is one F_q-linear system in (w, γ);
  - n = 4 gives 6 lines, n = 6 gives 12(q+1), and n = 2 gives none generically.

  - C4 PASS: dead points at chance (10/689, 3/4,242).
  - C5 PASS: column collisions at chance (75 against 81.1, 101 against 116.2), with the planted control exact.

  - C1 FAIL: one (13,4) curve gives a 19-line pencil, because one system has nullity 3.
  - C3 FAIL: one (101,2) curve has j ∈ F_q by chance (the descent case).

## 04:25Z — Lift-dense conjugate-pair family (Claude)

## BTN prime study (#2888): held-out pruning-plan rule

### What was done
Merged main (with #3522) into the #2888 branch so the study tool builds against the derived-last-slot crate. Added `rulecheck`: counts the crate's `decomposition_network` and the general network (semantic-cut path) with the pruning plan on and off, and checks the rule "build the plan only when 2^(free bits)·8 ≥ edges". p = 5, 13 (sizes used to choose the rule) and p = 67, 131 (d = 7, 8, held out), τ = s and s/8: correct in 11 of 12, worst 1.01× the best choice (p=67, τ=s), all counts agree. Where the rule switches the plan off on the crate's network: 1.83×, 3.84×, 1.28×, 1.53× fewer charged steps. Report, README, report.json (`pruning_rule`) updated.

### Decisions made
Only a small-instance gain: at cryptographic sizes the rule always builds the plan. Worth porting to `Counter` as a default (counts unchanged).

### Open threads
Crate port of the rule; cryptanalysis mirror re-sync.

### Errors
First attempt edited the wrong checkout (the study tool is only on the #2888 branch); disk fell to 153 MB, freed by removing the clippy debug build.

## Pruning-plan rule tried in the crate and dropped

### What was done
Added `Counter::adaptive_pruning` (default on: build the plan only when 2^(free bits)·8 ≥ edges) to `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/contraction.rs`, a README note and a test on the tiny decomposition network (counts and witness equal the forced-plan control, all 2^free assignments visited, fewer charged steps). The 23 contraction tests and the new test passed, but the full suite failed one test: `tests/structured.rs` `exact_counts_and_prefix_witnesses_match_all_subgroup_targets_with_and_without_messages` hit `Limit("parsimonious program evaluation")` on the isogeny-fibre `Prepared` network at arity 3 (arity 2 passed). With the plan off its count exceeded the 500,000,000-step budget.

### Decisions made
Dropped the crate change (never pushed) instead of weakening the test. A rule that sees only network size cannot predict per-assignment evaluation cost, which differs by network family. #2888's report and README now record the counterexample.

### Open threads
A sound rule would need a cost estimate per assignment (for example program steps until the first input-independent check), not edges alone.

### Errors
The held-out check covered only decomposition networks; the crate's other network family was the counterexample.

  - the difference is Weil descent with an F_2-linear Frobenius, which binary curves have and F_p does not;
  - the prime side is closed (`LEAD-ICE-prime-field-semaev-solving-degree`);
  - the binary side's open question is whether the solving degree stays constant (`LEAD-ICE-descent-closure-degree-at-scale`), with the `C1` cell blocked at 217 GB dense.
- The user chose both follow-ups.

D was 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, the same as the fixed-prime staircase, and the null gave the same D at every t. Written up in `research/pkm_matched_prime_20261106/`.
- **Binary side.** `examples/dreg_closure --sparse 5` started on `C1` draw 0 (`research/dreg_closure_scale_20261016/draws/m3-19-7.jsonl`) under a 14 GB address limit. It was at 5.5 GB after 65 min and still running.

- The prime-field lead stays closed: the slope is +0.2 per step and the system equals the null.

## 2026-11-06T02:55:00Z — F4/F5: weighted grading for the k = 5 Joux–Vitse Edwards test (option 2 feasibility)

- PR #3496 (F6-IC few-candidate closure, opt-in parallel split) merged at 2026-11-05T22:48Z. Its branch was restarted from `main`.
- Profiled after the merge, on `main` at `ff30ef0ef2`. With the closure, `f6p` costs 38–79 ms per target, against 0.6–1.6 s for `f4`. The root elimination is 97 % of its word XORs, so the closure leaves the pair-index meet-in-the-middle scan.
- Feasibility check of the Joux–Vitse k = 5 Edwards decision, chosen by the user ("do option 2"):
  - Probe: the ignored test `weighted_probe` in `src/cryptanalysis/jv_quintic_edwards.rs`.
  - Instance: `p = 271`, three random residuals.
  - `f4_fp` costs 5.85·10⁷.
  - The Macaulay solve unweighted decides at degree 9, for 7.0·10⁷ (echelon).
  - With weights (1,2,3,4,2) it decides only at weighted degree 37: 28,981 × 26,618, 3.9·10¹⁰ multiplications.
  - Written up in `research/jv_weighted_grading_20261106/` (README, REPORT.pdf, figure, raw output).
- `gaudry_quartic::solve_system_w_inner` now reports "1 is not standard: inconsistent" separately from "a variable is not standard".

- Weighted grading is not a lever on this route: about 670× worse. The precomputation of target-independent parts was argued, not built: every trial lies in one fixed 105-monomial space, and its shape is already used by trace replay.
- No `benchmarks/` entry or record: no speedup and no benchmark claim.

- No F4/F5 lever in sight moves a leaderboard row. Remaining options are recorded in the PR: exhaustive search over the last bits of the plain GF(2) `f4` engine (a few times on that engine only), or leaving F4/F5.

- The first probe run stopped at weighted degree 16 on an outcome that merged two cases, and looked like a 3,300× win. Splitting the outcome showed it was the case that decides nothing.

## hashed-ecdl-tensor: derive the last slot in decomposition_network

Branch `claude/hashed-ecdl-derived-last-slot` from main f465f2fb1. `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/reduction.rs`: for cofactor one and the non-semantic-cut path, `decomposition_network` now builds slots 1..m−1 as free input points (each hash-checked before its addition, as before) and computes `A_m = target − (A_1+…+A_{m−1})` with `modular_subtract` and `point_add`, then hash-checks and marks it like every other slot. Same language (bijection), so counts and the canonical witness are unchanged; free input bits drop from 2wm to 2w(m−1). The cofactor and semantic-cut paths are untouched. New test `derived_last_slot_matches_general_network_and_brute_force` (m=2 at three thresholds over every subgroup target, m=3 at one threshold): counts equal to the general network (semantic-cut path) and to an independent brute force, identical canonical witnesses, fewer free bits. Full crate suite: 140 tests pass (`cargo test --locked --release`). `cargo fmt --check` clean. Clippy clean except a pre-existing `clippy::manual_option_zip` in `src/canonical.rs` that only rustc 1.97's clippy reports (main's CI passes). End to end on `examples/fixture.json` (seed 1): scalar 4 in both, certificates byte-identical (13 relations, `verify` passes), charged steps 30,951,678 → 3,486,804 (8.9×), functional assignments 3,835 → 559; unisolated wall time 14.4 s → 1.05 s, a diagnostic only.

Default-on: outputs are identical, only the work drops. Cofactor > 1 keeps the general path because its free `S_i` preimage multiplicity would otherwise change raw counts. No cryptanalysis mirror in this PR: its copy of the crate is already ~370 lines behind crypto's in `reduction.rs` alone (last synced ~2026-10-30), so mirroring needs a full re-sync first.

## 2026-11-06T23:30:00Z — Binary vs prime polynomial systems: matched-prime PKM run; C1 degree-5 closure started

### What was done
- The user asked whether prime-field and binary curves differ in their polynomial systems in a way that can be exploited. Read the lead atlas (crypto-autoresearcher `knowledge/leads/ecdlp`):
  - the difference is Weil descent with an F_2-linear Frobenius, which binary curves have and F_p does not;
  - the prime side is closed (`LEAD-ICE-prime-field-semaev-solving-degree`);
  - the binary side's open question is whether the solving degree stays constant (`LEAD-ICE-descent-closure-degree-at-scale`), with the `C1` cell blocked at 217 GB dense.
- The user chose both follow-ups.
- **Prime side.** `examples/pkm_tower_pilot.rs` (m = 2, Kummer, tower and null) ran on primes matched to the depth: t = 5–9, p = 2,081 to 524,801. D was 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, the same as the fixed-prime staircase, and the null gave the same D at every t. Written up in `research/pkm_matched_prime_20261106/`.
- **Binary side.** `examples/dreg_closure --sparse 5` started on `C1` draw 0 (`research/dreg_closure_scale_20261016/draws/m3-19-7.jsonl`) under a 14 GB address limit. It was at 5.5 GB after 65 min and still running.

### Decisions made
- The prime-field lead stays closed: the slope is +0.2 per step and the system equals the null.
- `C1`: the sparse closure is tried first. If it caps, a degree-capped Boolean F4 is the remaining route, at several days' work, and the user is asked first.

### Open threads
- The `C1` sparse closure result, then draws 3, 5 and 7 if draw 0 completes.

### Errors
- The first sparse run "capped" in 0.2 s: `build_macaulay_sparse` honours `F4_F2_MAX_ROWS` / `F4_F2_MAX_COLS` (defaults 20,000 / 40,000). It was rerun with the protocol's 5·10⁷.
- The first PKM run panicked on the default `--ladder-t 4,6`, which needs 2^6 | p − 1. It was rerun with `--ladder-t t`.

## hashed-ecdl-tensor: derive the last slot in decomposition_network

### What was done
Branch `claude/hashed-ecdl-derived-last-slot` from main f465f2fb1. `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/reduction.rs`: for cofactor one and the non-semantic-cut path, `decomposition_network` now builds slots 1..m−1 as free input points (each hash-checked before its addition, as before) and computes `A_m = target − (A_1+…+A_{m−1})` with `modular_subtract` and `point_add`, then hash-checks and marks it like every other slot. Same language (bijection), so counts and the canonical witness are unchanged; free input bits drop from 2wm to 2w(m−1). The cofactor and semantic-cut paths are untouched. New test `derived_last_slot_matches_general_network_and_brute_force` (m=2 at three thresholds over every subgroup target, m=3 at one threshold): counts equal to the general network (semantic-cut path) and to an independent brute force, identical canonical witnesses, fewer free bits. Full crate suite: 140 tests pass (`cargo test --locked --release`). `cargo fmt --check` clean. Clippy clean except a pre-existing `clippy::manual_option_zip` in `src/canonical.rs` that only rustc 1.97's clippy reports (main's CI passes). End to end on `examples/fixture.json` (seed 1): scalar 4 in both, certificates byte-identical (13 relations, `verify` passes), charged steps 30,951,678 → 3,486,804 (8.9×), functional assignments 3,835 → 559; unisolated wall time 14.4 s → 1.05 s, a diagnostic only.

### Decisions made
Default-on: outputs are identical, only the work drops. Cofactor > 1 keeps the general path because its free `S_i` preimage multiplicity would otherwise change raw counts. No cryptanalysis mirror in this PR: its copy of the crate is already ~370 lines behind crypto's in `reduction.rs` alone (last synced ~2026-10-30), so mirroring needs a full re-sync first.

### Open threads
Re-sync the cryptanalysis mirror (suggested task; queuing timed out, unconfirmed). Adaptive pruning-plan rule and lean first slot from #2888 not ported.

`git grep` on the blobless sparse clone started fetching blobs on a nearly full disk; stopped it and read files via `git show` / the API instead.

## 03:15Z — v3a1 qualification failed in the launcher; run-request PATH fix (Claude)

### What was done
- The owner chose option 2 (MCP-confirmed receipt). I wrote the receipt with check-experiment-git's own input checks: 9 inputs at f2467699, with GitHub confirmation through MCP get_commit. The checkpoint was pushed and `scripts/checkpoint.sh gate` exits 0. An expired CHECKPOINT_UPLOAD_TOKEN in the environment had to be unset; the gate then used the AWS identity.
- Card CARD-IC-LINE-LAYOUT-V3A1-01 (director), run unchanged by executor-mechanical, launched job ic-line-v3a1-qual-20261106 at 03:01:06Z, CodeBuild d6270339-9648-4adc-ab66-56f1374c9f3c.
- Result at 03:02:56Z: `state: launcher_failed`, exit 127, no job_uid and no pod_uid, so no EKS job was created. The build log shows `run-request.override: line 44: isolab-eks-mcp: command not found`.
- Root cause: since a34125841 (2026-11-01), launch-remote overrides the project buildspec with `current-run-request-buildspec.yml`. That buildspec omits the default's `export PATH="$CODEBUILD_SRC_DIR/bin:$PATH"`, so the packaged `bin/isolab-eks-mcp` is not on PATH. `run-command` already carries this export with a comment; `run-request` did not.
- Fix: add the same export to `remote/run-request`, plus a regression check in `remote/test-launch-remote.sh`. Without the fix the check exits 1 ("run-request does not put the launcher bin/ on PATH"); with it the test exits 0. `test-launch-remote-command.sh` still passes.

### Decisions made
- Protocol v4 stopping rule 1 applies: the qualification failed and is not retried, so evidence version 4 stops before the tournament. No scientific seed was consumed and no pod ran. Rerunning needs a new amendment and the owner's decision.

### Open threads
- Merge the run-request fix. If the owner agrees, file v3 amendment 2 (a new qualification job name, otherwise unchanged) and rerun.
- isolab-experiment.yml also passes this override (a34125841 touched it). The GitHub-route failures since 2026-11-02 may share this cause; not checked.

- Feasibility check of the Joux–Vitse k = 5 Edwards decision, chosen by the user ("do option 2"):

  - With weights (1,2,3,4,2) it decides only at weighted degree 37: 28,981 × 26,618, 3.9·10¹⁰ multiplications.

## hashed-ecdl-tensor: derive the last slot in decomposition_network

Branch `claude/hashed-ecdl-derived-last-slot` from main f465f2fb1. `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/reduction.rs`: for cofactor one and the non-semantic-cut path, `decomposition_network` now builds slots 1..m−1 as free input points (each hash-checked before its addition, as before) and computes `A_m = target − (A_1+…+A_{m−1})` with `modular_subtract` and `point_add`, then hash-checks and marks it like every other slot. Same language (bijection), so counts and the canonical witness are unchanged; free input bits drop from 2wm to 2w(m−1). The cofactor and semantic-cut paths are untouched. New test `derived_last_slot_matches_general_network_and_brute_force` (m=2 at three thresholds over every subgroup target, m=3 at one threshold): counts equal to the general network (semantic-cut path) and to an independent brute force, identical canonical witnesses, fewer free bits. Full crate suite: 140 tests pass (`cargo test --locked --release`). `cargo fmt --check` clean. Clippy clean except a pre-existing `clippy::manual_option_zip` in `src/canonical.rs` that only rustc 1.97's clippy reports (main's CI passes). End to end on `examples/fixture.json` (seed 1): scalar 4 in both, certificates byte-identical (13 relations, `verify` passes), charged steps 30,951,678 → 3,486,804 (8.9×), functional assignments 3,835 → 559; unisolated wall time 14.4 s → 1.05 s, a diagnostic only.

Default-on: outputs are identical, only the work drops. Cofactor > 1 keeps the general path because its free `S_i` preimage multiplicity would otherwise change raw counts. `input_point` validates A1, then `point_add` validates −A1, which holds exactly when A1 is valid (same x; `modular_subtract` makes y canonical; (−y)² = y²). Added a `lean` variant building A1 from raw input words, and a `lean` mode comparing it with the combined derived network (pruning on/off, brute force, checked witness) on p = 5, 7, 11, 13 at τ = s, s/2, s/4, s/8 (32 instances). Edges 16,905→14,340 (d=3), 29,329→24,540 (d=4). All counts exact both ways, all witnesses checked. Best-of-pruning steps: lean 1.08–1.66× faster at τ ≤ s/4, 0.59–0.91× (slower) at τ ≥ s/2. Report section, README, report.json (`lean`) updated.

Report as threshold-dependent. The slowdown at large τ is because the curve check, which rejects most (x, y) pairs, then runs only inside `point_add`, after the hash and subtraction. Realistic factor bases (τ/s ≈ 2^-66 at ECCp-131) sit in the lean regime.

Crate port (derived last slot, adaptive pruning, lean first slot): paired crypto/cryptanalysis change.

`json!` macro rejected a block with a typed closure; computed the summary before the macro.

## BTN prime study (#2888): held-out pruning-plan rule

Merged main (with #3522) into the #2888 branch so the study tool builds against the derived-last-slot crate. Added `rulecheck`: counts the crate's `decomposition_network` and the general network (semantic-cut path) with the pruning plan on and off, and checks the rule "build the plan only when 2^(free bits)·8 ≥ edges". p = 5, 13 (sizes used to choose the rule) and p = 67, 131 (d = 7, 8, held out), τ = s and s/8: correct in 11 of 12, worst 1.01× the best choice (p=67, τ=s), all counts agree. Where the rule switches the plan off on the crate's network: 1.83×, 3.84×, 1.28×, 1.53× fewer charged steps. Report, README, report.json (`pruning_rule`) updated.

Only a small-instance gain: at cryptographic sizes the rule always builds the plan. Worth porting to `Counter` as a default (counts unchanged).

Crate port of the rule; cryptanalysis mirror re-sync.

First attempt edited the wrong checkout (the study tool is only on the #2888 branch); disk fell to 153 MB, freed by removing the clippy debug build.

## Pruning-plan rule tried in the crate and dropped

Added `Counter::adaptive_pruning` (default on: build the plan only when 2^(free bits)·8 ≥ edges) to `crates/hashed-ecdl-tensor/src/contraction.rs`, a README note and a test on the tiny decomposition network (counts and witness equal the forced-plan control, all 2^free assignments visited, fewer charged steps). The 23 contraction tests and the new test passed, but the full suite failed one test: `tests/structured.rs` `exact_counts_and_prefix_witnesses_match_all_subgroup_targets_with_and_without_messages` hit `Limit("parsimonious program evaluation")` on the isogeny-fibre `Prepared` network at arity 3 (arity 2 passed). With the plan off its count exceeded the 500,000,000-step budget.

Dropped the crate change (never pushed) instead of weakening the test. A rule that sees only network size cannot predict per-assignment evaluation cost, which differs by network family. #2888's report and README now record the counterexample.

A sound rule would need a cost estimate per assignment (for example program steps until the first input-independent check), not edges alone.

The held-out check covered only decomposition networks; the crate's other network family was the counterexample.
